partner_context.their_ambition: Metlink is the public-transport authority for the Wellington region — train, bus and the harbour ferry — and it already runs the Southern Hemisphere's first fully electric passenger ferry, Ika Rere, on the harbour. Its ambition on the water is a fully decarbonised harbour network that connects Queens Wharf to Days Bay, Matiu/Somes and Seatoun, and it has set the region on a path to a zero-emission public-transport fleet.
partner_context.where_navier_fits: Navier is the foiling-electric next step for a harbour network Metlink has already started to electrify. The cross-harbour commute to Days Bay, the island stop at Matiu/Somes and the Seatoun link — flown clear of one of the world's windiest, choppiest harbours: faster, smoother, near-silent and zero-emission, on the same Metlink ticket, from the wharves that already exist.

hero.eyebrow: Authority proposal · Wellington, New Zealand · Metlink (Greater Wellington Regional Council)
hero.title: Navier × Wellington Ferries — the harbour, on foils
hero.subtitle: A zero-emission foiling layer on Metlink's harbour ferry — Queens Wharf to Days Bay, Matiu/Somes and Seatoun: faster, smoother and all-electric across a harbour Metlink already runs on the Southern Hemisphere's first electric ferry.
hero.what_we_do_together: Metlink brings the harbour ferry network, the wharves and the public-transport mandate; Navier brings the foiling-electric fleet, captain training and the certification path. Together we run the same harbour — faster, smoother and zero-emission — building on the electric ferry Metlink has already put in service.

why_now: Metlink already operates Ika Rere, the Southern Hemisphere's first fully electric passenger ferry, and is committed to a zero-emission fleet inside a country legally bound to net-zero by 2050. The precedent is set and the wharves are in place; a foiling ride is also how a notoriously rough harbour crossing becomes fast and smooth, not just clean.
multimodal_fit: Navier slots into the Metlink network at Queens Wharf, steps from the railway station and the bus interchange. A commuter steps off the train and straight onto a foil across the harbour to Days Bay or Seatoun — a faster, smoother, zero-emission crossing on the same Metlink ticket.

journeys_unlocked.label: Seatoun ↔ Matiu/Somes Island
journeys_unlocked.today: A limited harbour hop to the predator-free island reserve.
journeys_unlocked.with_navier: A low-wake, near-silent link that protects Matiu/Somes' restored habitat while connecting it cleanly to the network.

journeys_unlocked.label: Queens Wharf ↔ Days Bay
journeys_unlocked.today: The cross-harbour commuter run to Eastbourne — slow and often rough on a windy day.
journeys_unlocked.with_navier: The flagship commute, flown clear of the chop — fast, smooth, near-silent and zero-emission across a famously rough harbour.

journeys_unlocked.label: Queens Wharf ↔ Seatoun
journeys_unlocked.today: A seasonal, low-frequency link to the eastern bays.
journeys_unlocked.with_navier: A direct clean link to Seatoun and the eastern bays, made viable year-round by foiling range and ride quality.

differentiation.why_navier: The platform is purpose-built for this network: 10x more efficient than a planing hull, low-wake (vital on shared and protected waters), near-silent, zero-emission, and viable year-round. It delivers the authority's published decarbonisation commitment on the links where speed and wake have kept older vessels in service.

proof_points.claim: Metlink already runs an electric ferry.
proof_points.evidence: Ika Rere, operating on the Wellington harbour ferry, is the Southern Hemisphere's first fully electric passenger ferry — part of the Metlink fleet.

proof_points.claim: The harbour ferry is public transport.
proof_points.evidence: The Queens Wharf–Days Bay–Matiu/Somes–Seatoun service runs on the Metlink public-transport network and ticket.
New Zealand's Zero Carbon Act commits the country to net-zero by 2050, with regional councils driving public-transport decarbonisation.
proof_points.source: NZ Climate Change Response (Zero Carbon) Amendment Act

proof_points.claim: The platform is proven in service.
proof_points.evidence: 10 vessels delivered, 4,000+ flight hours, 2025 production sold out.

objections.concern: Can it handle Wellington's wind and chop?
objections.response: That's the point — flying clear of the surface, a foiling hull delivers a markedly smoother, more reliable ride than a planing hull in exactly the harbour conditions Wellington is known for.

objections.concern: Does it disturb the island reserve?
objections.response: The opposite — low wake and near-silent running reduce disturbance to Matiu/Somes' predator-free habitat compared with today's vessels.

objections.concern: Does this replace Ika Rere and the ferries people rely on?
objections.response: No — it's a faster, smoother layer on the same Metlink ticket; the existing electric and diesel ferries keep the core service.

the_ask.navier_brings: The software-defined foiling-electric fleet, captain training, and the maintenance and certification path.
the_ask.partner_brings: The ferry route map, the piers/stops, the single-ticket integration, and the published decarbonisation mandate.
the_ask.next_step: Identify the first Metlink harbour link — most likely Queens Wharf–Days Bay — for a foiling-electric public pilot on the Metlink ticket.

close.body: Metlink already gave Wellington the Southern Hemisphere's first electric ferry. Navier is the next step — a fast, smooth, zero-emission crossing to Days Bay, Matiu/Somes and Seatoun, on the same public ticket, tamed to one of the world's roughest commuter harbours.
